correctness.rationale: The standard realization has total coordinate sum 2^n-1. Every proper tube facet has an offset obtained by counting Minkowski summands contained in that tube. All singleton facets have offset zero and intrinsic normal norm sqrt(n/(n+1)); summing their ball constraints gives the sharp radius upper bound and forces the unique uniform center at equality. For a center-containing tube of size k, its exact distance is reduced to inequality (19). That inequality follows from the monotonicity of (2^(j-1)-1)/(j(j-1)) and the elementary bound k(N-k)/(N-1)>=1. The equality analysis leaves only singleton facets for n>=3 and the two additional size-two facets when n=2.

value.rationale: The stellohedron is a canonical graph associahedron with exponentially many facets and an active recent literature on its combinatorics and related parking-function realizations. The finding gives its exact canonical Euclidean size, proves an unexpectedly uniform unique incenter despite the star center being combinatorially distinguished, and shows that for every dimension at least three only the n+1 singleton facets control the maximal ball. It also separates Euclidean realization from mere combinatorial equivalence with partial permutohedra, making the metric statement structurally informative rather than a routine facet-distance calculation.
